title: NumPy: 3D Tensors & Broadcasting
subtitle: Vectorized N-D Arrays, Slicing & Axis Reductions
summary: Inspect 3D tensor shapes, stride slicing, broadcasting expansion, and axis=0/1/2 reductions in 3D.

evaluationChart.title: Execution Speed: Python Loop vs. NumPy Vectorized (100k Ops)
evaluationChart.description: Contiguous C-backed ndarray memory and SIMD vectorization eliminate Python interpreter loop overhead.

advantages: Contiguous typed memory layout enables 50x–100x faster SIMD vectorized math than Python lists.
Broadcasting aligns mismatched tensor shapes virtually without copying memory.
Universal interchange format underlying Pandas, Scikit-Learn, and PyTorch.
limitations: CPU-only execution (use PyTorch/CuPy for CUDA GPU acceleration).
Fixed homogeneous dtype per ndarray (unlike mixed-type Pandas DataFrames).
Large unintended broadcasts can silently allocate gigabytes of RAM.

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

X = np.arange(48).reshape(3, 4, 4)
print('Shape:', X.shape, 'Strides:', X.strides)

# Broadcasting (3, 4, 1) + (1, 1, 4) -> (3, 4, 4)
bias = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40])
Y = X + bias
print('Axis 0 sum shape:', Y.sum(axis=0).shape)
